market_question: Will the No to ten million Switzerland initiative be approved in Switzerland’s June 14, 2026 popular vote?
reasoning: Swiss popular initiatives historically have a low success rate (~10%), and the 'No to 10 Million' proposal faces broad opposition from the Federal Council and most parties. The double‑majority requirement further reduces the chance of approval. While immigration concerns are high, similar SVP‑led initiatives have failed in recent years, making a Yes outcome unlikely.
evidence_points: Fewer than 10% of Swiss popular initiatives are approved; the most comparable recent SVP-inspired measures lost.
The initiative requires a double majority (popular vote + majority of cantons), a high bar that this proposal has not previously cleared.
The Federal Council and the large center/left parties are poised to recommend rejection and campaign against it.
Parliament may also propose a weaker counter‑proposal, splitting support and making outright approval harder.
sources_consulted: Historical Swiss initiative passage rates and voting patterns
Standard Swiss Federal Chancellery voting procedures
Recent Swiss referenda outcomes on immigration-related measures
